mappings.note: Defines a maritime neighbour as a country joined by a shared sea rather than a land border - a spatial-relationship concept. Goal-level CG-SST1 (earth as habitat, spatial distribution): LO-4 is specifically climatic regions on a map and cannot take political geography. (Answer key on this row is internally inconsistent; see report.)

India's peninsular projection giving it command of routes linking Southeast Asia, West Asia and Africa. Spatial position and its consequences, so goal-level CG-SST1; LO-2 is rejected because nothing about how the peninsula formed is asked.

Identifies the northern belt - Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Ladakh - as the China frontier. Pure location, goal-level CG-SST1, since LO-4 covers only climatic regions. (Stored answer is truncated and then continues with unrelated Suvarnabhumi text; see report.)

Reads Tamil's official status in Singapore as evidence of long South Indian migration and exchange - an inference from present-day evidence about the past. Goal-level CG-SST2; no LO covers migration or cultural diffusion.
Two-mark recall of the maritime-neighbour definition with Sri Lanka, Maldives, Indonesia and Oman as instances. Goal-level CG-SST1 for the spatial concept.

Evaluates the Kartarpur Corridor as a model for dialogue between two states. Goal-level CG-SST4, the only goal naming government as an institution; this frame has no international-relations outcome at all, which is the gap being worked around.

Defines an open border and grounds it in the India-Nepal arrangement that lets families move for education, work and worship. Goal-level CG-SST4 because the content is a government policy shaping everyday socio-economic life.

Three-mark version of the maritime-neighbour question, requiring Sri Lanka across the Palk Strait and Thailand across the Bay of Bengal. Same goal-level CG-SST1 as the definition items; the distances and directions are what is scored.

How Buddhism built links with Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bhutan, Myanmar, Tibet and Southeast Asia. LO-12 covers the emergence and spread of religious ideas and movements; LO-13 is rejected outright, being bhakti and sufi poetry.

Open border policy and its effect on cross-border education, healthcare, employment and family life. Goal-level CG-SST4; the daily-life consequence is socio-economic, not spatial, which is why CG-SST1 is rejected here but used for the border-location items.
Names the Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal and Indian Ocean from a map. Map reading, but of water bodies, so goal-level CG-SST1 rather than LO-4, which is confined to climatic regions.

A samudra manthana relief at an airport named Suvarnabhumi, and what that name recalls about 3rd-century-BCE Indian voyages to Southeast Asia. Historical contact evidenced in present naming; goal-level CG-SST2.

'Being neighbours is not just about geography', answered through Buddhism, scholarly exchange and the Silk Route alongside present-day relations. CG-SST2 for the historical ties, CG-SST4 for the contemporary state-to-state dimension; neither has an LO that reaches this.

India's assistance to neighbours - temple restoration in Myanmar, the Afghan parliament and Zaranj-Delaram highway, relief to the Maldives. Goal-level CG-SST4 for government acting beyond its borders.

Shared challenges producing cooperation, illustrated by the post-2004 tsunami sensor network and the Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre. LO-6 is a genuine fit: preventive action in the event of disaster, its 'such as' list being open.

Imagines a map drawn by culture rather than politics - Hinduism to Nepal, Buddhism and the Ramayana to Southeast Asia, trade and language to West Asia. Cultural diffusion over time, goal-level CG-SST2.

The India-China trade balance, China's exports being worth roughly eight times India's. Goal-level CG-SST4 for the market dimension; C-SST4.2 is rejected because that competency is local markets visited in person.

The Kartarpur Corridor's purpose: visa-free pilgrim access to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib. Goal-level CG-SST4 as a bilateral government arrangement; LO-12 is rejected because no religious idea or movement is being explained.
Why the open border matters for people living near it - free movement for education, healthcare and work. Goal-level CG-SST4, same reasoning as the other open-border items.

Distinguishes Vajrayana's esoteric teachings and mandalas from Theravada's adherence to the Buddha's original path. Two schools as distinct religious developments - LO-12, not LO-11, since nothing architectural is tested.

Match-list pairing Sri Lanka with the Palk Strait and the Maldives with its 1,100 islands (location, CG-SST1) against Ayutthaya from Ayodhya and Tamil in Singapore (cultural transmission, CG-SST2). Both halves must be known. (Stem survives only as its last line; see report.)

Match-list of SAARC, the Kartarpur Corridor, the International Solar Alliance and the India-Myanmar land border agreement - four intergovernmental instruments. Goal-level CG-SST4 throughout. (Fragmentary stem; see report.)

Match-list mixing Pashupatinath, the Bagan restoration and Borobudur (religious monuments, LO-11) with the Sundarban as the world's largest mangrove forest (flora conservation, LO-8). Both codes are needed to score the row. (Fragmentary stem; see report.)

Match-list of Bodhidharma to China, Padmasambhava to Bhutan and Mahendra and Sanghamitra to Sri Lanka (transmission of a religious movement, LO-12) plus Uttarapatha as a trade route (CG-SST2, no LO covering ancient routes). (Fragmentary stem; see report.)

Thailand's Dvaravati culture named from Dvaraka, Krishna's city in the Mahabharata. Cultural and linguistic transmission; goal-level CG-SST2, since LO-12 would require a religious movement rather than a place name.
The 2004 tsunami driving India, Indonesia, Sri Lanka and Thailand into a shared sensor and warning network. Preventive action against disaster, LO-6, which is a real fit rather than a fallback.
The Avesta's parallels with the Rigveda. A question about two ancient texts and shared Indo-Iranian heritage, so goal-level CG-SST2; LO-12 is rejected because no new movement is being explained.
Defines an ingot as a cast metal block for bulk transport, a vocabulary item serving the Harappan copper trade. Goal-level CG-SST2; no LO covers ancient commerce.
Myanmar as India's land gateway to Southeast Asia. Location and its strategic consequence, goal-level CG-SST1.

Assertion-reason on Bhutan's rivers underpinning hydroelectric generation for both countries. LO-8 for the renewable-energy and water strand it names explicitly; CG-SST1 for a resource distributed across a border.

Guru Padmasambhava introducing Vajrayana to Bhutan in the 8th century. The arrival of a new religious school, LO-12; distinguished from the Vajrayana-versus-Theravada item only by what is recalled, not by outcome.

Bhutan's Gross National Happiness Index as an alternative measure of progress built on sustainability, governance and culture. Goal-level CG-SST4 for a governance instrument; LO-8 is rejected because conservation is one component, not the question.
India's gift of a Sarnath Buddha replica to the Shwedagon Pagoda. LO-11 to identify the monument among Borobudur, Kaiyuan and Pashupatinath; CG-SST4 because the act itself is cultural diplomacy.
The Bamiyan Buddhas as the monument an archaeologist would study for Mahayana's reach into Afghanistan. LO-11 for the carved monument, LO-12 for the spread of the school it evidences.
Suvarnabhumi translated as the Golden Land, the name Indian traders gave Java and Sumatra. Historical naming and contact, goal-level CG-SST2.
Buddhism reaching China around the 1st century CE by trade and pilgrimage routes rather than conquest. The mechanism by which a religious movement spread, LO-12.
The Kaiyuan temple at Quanzhou, whose pillars carry Vishnu, Shiva and Ramayana scenes. Distinctive temple construction and decoration, a direct LO-11 fit.

The Sundarban as the world's largest mangrove forest, jointly managed by India and Bangladesh, and acting as a cyclone barrier. LO-8 for conserving the forest, LO-6 for the protection it gives against a disaster. (Fragmentary stem; see report.)

The Sundarban National Park as the shared zone most exposed to sea-level rise. LO-8, sensitivity to conserving flora and fauna; LO-6 is rejected because no preventive action is named, only the vulnerability.
The 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship as the instrument behind the India-Nepal open border, discriminated from SAARC and the Indus Waters Treaty. Goal-level CG-SST4.

Pashupatinath in Kathmandu as the Hindu pilgrimage drawing Indian visitors. Cited at competency level: LO-11 would require its architecture and LO-12 a religious movement, whereas this tests a living religious tie, which C-SST2.3 frames but no LO under it reaches.
Bangladesh emerging in 1971. A dated historical event; goal-level CG-SST2, whose competencies stop at medieval kingdoms and so cannot take twentieth-century history.
Why India lost its direct land link to Afghanistan - the creation of Pakistan in 1947. CG-SST2 for the event, CG-SST1 for the resulting spatial fact that a third state now lies between them.
The Thai kingdom of Ayutthaya named for Ayodhya under the Ramayana's influence. Cultural transmission, goal-level CG-SST2.
Singapore from Singapuram, 'lion city'. Sanskrit-derived place naming, goal-level CG-SST2.

Borobudur's geometry read as a three-dimensional mandala representing the cosmos. Distinctive style and technology of a religious monument - LO-11 exactly, not LO-12, since the question is architectural.
India's land boundary of over 15,100 km across deserts, forests and mountains. Spatial extent, goal-level CG-SST1.
Dhivehi as the Maldivian language, noted for borrowing heavily from South Indian languages. Linguistic evidence of long contact, goal-level CG-SST2.
Which neighbour reaches Male first with water, medicine and rescue teams after a tsunami. Disaster response, LO-6 - a real fit, the 2004 tsunami and 2014 water crisis being the cited precedents.

A projected one-metre sea-level rise threatening the Maldives. Cited at competency level: LO-6 asks for preventive action and LO-8 for conservation behaviour, whereas this tests the scale of a hazard, which only C-SST1.3 as a whole covers.
The India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway improving overland connectivity and regional trade. Goal-level CG-SST4 for a state-built trade artery.
South Indian labour migration to Malaysian rubber plantations in the 19th and 20th centuries. Historical migration, goal-level CG-SST2.

Assertion-reason tying Tamil signage in Singapore to the roughly 9 percent of residents of Indian origin. The reason is historical migration, so goal-level CG-SST2 rather than any CG-SST4 market reading.
Defines an archipelago, with Indonesia's 17,000 islands as the instance. A physical-geography term; goal-level CG-SST1 because LO-2 asks how landforms form, which this does not.

Nalanda's collaboration with the Muara Jambi complex in Indonesia. Historical scholarly exchange, goal-level CG-SST2; LO-11 is rejected because the complex is named as an institution, not described architecturally.
The Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre in Hyderabad as the body alerting neighbours to a Sumatran seafloor quake. Preventive action against disaster, LO-6.

Oman as Harappan copper source, maritime neighbour, and home to an early-twentieth-century Shiva temple and a large Indian community. The through-line is millennia of contact, so goal-level CG-SST2. (Fragmentary stem; see report.)
India developing Chabahar in Iran for access to Afghanistan and Central Asia. A state infrastructure and trade project, goal-level CG-SST4.
Copper ingots carried back from Oman by Harappan traders in the 3rd millennium BCE. Archaeological trade evidence, goal-level CG-SST2.

Katas Raj, the Mahabharata-linked temple complex, located in Pakistan's Punjab. Competency-level C-SST2.3 for a shared sacred site: LO-11 would need its architecture and LO-12 a religious movement, neither of which the stem asks for.
